title: sign_op.sig_len not bounded against CRYPTO2DEV_SIG_MAXLEN
description:
After CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_DO_SIGN ioctl, sign_op.sig_len is validated only against *info->pk.eccsign.outlen (line 1365) before XMEMCPY. It is not validated against CRYPTO2DEV_SIG_MAXLEN (512).

If the kernel returns sig_len > 512 (malicious or buggy driver) and outlen >= sig_len, XMEMCPY(out, sign_op.sig, sig_len) reads beyond the 512-byte sign_op.sig[] stack array → stack buffer overread.

In practice, ECDSA signatures are much smaller (P-256 DER = ~72 bytes) and outlen is bounded by the caller, so the outlen check fires first. But the CRYPTO2DEV_SIG_MAXLEN bound should be checked as a kernel-trust boundary.

Fix: add 'if (sign_op.sig_len > CRYPTO2DEV_SIG_MAXLEN) return BUFFER_E;' before the outlen check, analogous to the eccverify path's verify_op.sig_len check (line 1408).
